## My pick: JBL Charge 6

It's the best all-rounder for pool or beach. It has an IP68 rating, a rugged build, and strong, clear sound. It can also charge your phone. Battery life is listed as 20 hours (28 with Playtime Boost) by [What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart), which shows it at $129.99 at Walmart and $149.95 at Amazon. [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) listed it at $150, down from $200. Prices change, so check the retailer before you buy.

## Other good options

| Need | Pick | Why | Price seen |
|---|---|---|---|
| Loud pool party | JBL Boombox 4 | RTINGS' top waterproof pick. It floats, handles long immersion, and lasts 40+ hours. Its sound is narrow, so it's weaker if you're off to the side. ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth)) | Not listed |
| 360° sound while you swim | Ultimate Ears EPICBOOM | IP67, floats, and sounds the same from every side. Battery is about 15 hours. Tom's Guide's best overall. ([Tom's Guide](https://www.tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-waterproof-speakers)) | Not listed |
| Budget | Ultimate Ears WONDERBOOM 4 | IP67, floats, and has 360° sound. It's small, so it's less loud. About 14 hours of battery. ([BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/)) | $65–$80 |
| Easy to carry | JBL Grip | Best overall in Good Housekeeping's test. It's can-sized, under a pound, and IP68, with 12 hours of battery. The mesh can look dusty after beach use. ([Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/)) | $100 |
| Cheapest | JBL Go 5 | Pocket-sized and IP67, but only about 8 hours of battery. ([What Hi-Fi](https://www.whathifi.com/best-buys/best-waterproof-speakers-around-right-now-budget-portable-smart)) | $39.95 |
| Big party on a budget | Soundcore Boom 2 Plus | 100 W, IPX7, floats, and about 20 hours at half volume with lights off. It weighs 3.8 kg (about 8.4 lb). The $249.99 price drops to about $200 with code AFSC20, which Dealectric says it tested on 2026-10-22. [Buy at Soundcore via Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/go/soundcore-boom-2-plus). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric earns a commission. ([listing](https://dealectric.com/soundcore-boom-2-plus)) | $249.99 |

Soundcore's own sources disagree on whether the Boom 2 Plus has Bluetooth 6.0 or 5.3. The smaller Soundcore Boom 2 is about $110 and floats, but it has no dust rating. [BestProducts](https://www.bestproducts.com/tech/gadgets/g938/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers/) says to keep it on a towel at the beach.

## Tips for pool and beach use

- **IP ratings don't cover salt or chlorine.** RTINGS recommends rinsing with fresh water after use, because chlorine and salt wear down the surface over time, especially fabric. Check your manual first, since some advise against beach or pool use. ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/speaker/reviews/best/by-type/waterproof-bluetooth))
- **Look for IP67 or higher.** For the beach, an IP6X dust rating also helps keep sand out. ([Good Housekeeping](https://www.goodhousekeeping.com/what-to-buy/a71783745/best-waterproof-speakers/))
- **Close the charging port flap** and dry the speaker fully before charging. ([iTechGuides](https://www.itechguides.com/best-waterproof-bluetooth-speakers-for-the-beach-pool-and-shower/))

The search results only gave me one direct purchase link, the Soundcore one above. For the others, the review pages linked above have current retailer buttons.

If you tell me your budget and how loud you need it, I can narrow this to one pick.
